Got an original painting or photo you’re just tired of looking at? Bring it to the WMAA and trade it for an entirely new one. You’ll receive a numbered ticket for your piece, which will be displayed in the museum’s McKenna Gallery until 7pm, when tickets will be pulled to begin the swap. Once your number is drawn, you’ll have 30 seconds to select a new artwork. 

No piece to share? No time to create one? No problem. Use the studio space to get your Van Gogh on and prepare a piece during the event. Canvas, paint and brushes will be available to serve your artistic genius.

by Seth LeDonne
Mixed media installation recapping and rearranging developmental experience and the various artforms it has anchored onto. An illustrative and introspective look into the suburban experience, touching on themes of slackerdom, idealism, and redemption. An assemblage emerging in the spot between accountability and intentionality. Presented through drawings, paintings, collage, film, and personal photographs.

data.description: On August 23, 2011, God called home one amazing, loved, young man. A tragic street bike accident on route 40 took a precious life away that will never be forgotten. Mark was 23 and going through what most of us would call a hard time in life. Though you'd never be able to tell by looking at him; He always had a smile on his face, accompanied by a heart filled laugh that was truly unlike any other you'd ever hear. It is so sad when such tragedies happen to people so young with such a bright future ahead of them. Please keep Mark and his family in your thoughts and prayers.  Rest easy angel. I love you with all my heart; your sister forever <3
data.name: RIP Mark. Prayers for Mark Gaydos & Family

data.description:
*CONCERT IS OPEN TO THE PUBLIC*

California University of Pennsylvania will kick off the 2011 football season with its sixth annual Party in the Park and a performance by the nationally known pop punk band Forever The Sickest Kids.

The party gets started at 3:30 p.m. Sept. 1 at Roadman Park on Cal U’s south campus. The public may attend.

The fun begins with a performance by the band Beyond Daylight and a Welcome Back Picnic hosted by University President Angelo Armenti, Jr. 

The menu includes salads; grilled hamburgers, hotdogs and chicken; corn on the cob from a local farm; desserts and beverages. Vegetarian options are available. Picnic guests pay $6.75 for adults, $3.75 for children age 7 and younger. Cal U students, faculty and staff may attend the picnic free with a valid CalCard.

An alumni tailgate party begins at 5 p.m. at the Roadman Park pavilions.

Forever The Sickest Kids will perform from 5-6:30 p.m. The AllMusic website says the band’s “songs are unapologetically catchy and simple, the ballads are heart-on-the-sleeve emotional, and the sound (is) arena-ready.”

The party wraps up with a 7 p.m. football game at Adamson Stadium’s Hepner-Bailey Field, where the nationally ranked Cal U Vulcans take on St. Cloud State (Minn.).

Game tickets are available at the gate. Cost is $8 for general admission seating. Cal U students with valid CalCards may attend the game at no charge; cost is $5 for students who do not attend Cal U.
data.name: BEYOND DAYLIGHT W/ FOREVER THE SICKEST KIDS (FREE SHOW)

You all know the heritage of NYC's lower east side. The richness of the underground that was once more is long lost. 

Our excitement in creating a new weekly Friday night party is focused on the elements that made the LES legend: Music, People, and most importantly, the Vibe. 

This vibe will be built on a foundation of nyc's most eclectic young professionals, artists and musicians, and friends. The sounds you'll hear will change every Friday, ranging from classics to current, but it won't be basic. On the decks will be the MWB Residents Kunal Merchant & Seif Al-Din, plus a rotating group of superfriends...

Our bar is be perfect - We'll have the favorites that you're fond of plus a diverse selection of custom cocktails. Most importantly, our prices will be fair. You won't leave feeling robbed. 

We look forward to seeing you this Friday and more after... If you are looking to celebrate a special occasion or just the end of the week, message any of our team and we'll take care of you.

Over the course of five days, five classic albums from five boroughs will be revisited in lectures and workshops throughout NYC. From September 25 – 30- Queens, Brooklyn, Bronx, Staten Island and Manhattan will be the landing spots for each lecture and performance that will pay homage to arguably the most influential youth culture of our time – Hip Hop – right where is all began. At night, the artists will re-create their seminal work for a concert in each respective borough, bridging the gap from old to new school hip-hop. 

Red Bull Music Academy has embarked on a World Tour going straight to the heart of today’s most crucial musical movements, and taking listeners beyond the beat. NYC iis one of 10 ground-breaking celebrations and explorations around the globe that will feature signature concerts, workshops, art installations, studio sessions and parties in extraordinary locations.
